tasks.short: Administer blood products and watch for transfusion reactions

steps.what: Check patient, prescribed blood products and bedside readiness
Administer blood and monitor patient for transfusion reactions

tasks.design: Retain bedside verification, administration and reaction assessment by the nurse. The {OTHER} clinical record and transfusion equipment support the existing procedure; a digital alarm does not replace observing the patient.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task depends on correct bedside actions and recognition of changing signs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical records can display the prescription, without removing the physical checks.
tasks.still_hard: A reaction can emerge during administration and needs immediate clinical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Notice deterioration, stop or escalate within the local procedure and explain events to the patient.
tasks.altitude: No change in clinical responsibility or bedside time.

reach.learn: Local verification, reaction escalation and handover requirements

evidence.claim: Bedside transfusion administration and assessment require physical nursing work; a record interface alone does not remove it.

assumptions: Boundary starts with an available prescription and issued blood product and ends with administration and immediate reaction monitoring; blood-bank preparation and prescribing remain outside and unchanged.

The prescriber produces patient identifier, product, dose and instructions; the blood bank produces product identifier and compatibility information. Their existing preparation time is unchanged outside this boundary; nurse reconciliation and bedside observations are counted in s1 and s2.
Unreadable, conflicting or missing information triggers the existing manual verification and escalation procedure, with no assumed time saving.
Check native clinical-record and transfusion-device functions before any custom development; none is proposed here.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new software, data capture or review process is introduced. Routine recording is counted elsewhere and earns no saving here.
unknowns: Local verification procedure, monitoring requirements and actual baseline times
research_questions: Does observed bedside work reveal any duplicate entry that belongs in a separate documentation task?

already_counted.description: All bedside verification, administration and monitoring remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross and net=0. Both uncomplicated transfusion and suspected reaction retain bedside work; no reduction from existing equipment runtime.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advocate for patients and families and provide emotional support

steps.what: Listen to patients and families and clarify their needs
Provide emotional support and advocate for agreed needs

tasks.design: Keep listening, emotional support and advocacy with the nurse. Use existing {OTHER} clinical-record access only when the nurse needs care context; a generated response is not a substitute for this interaction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs are expressed indirectly and can change during a difficult conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: No evidenced technology change removes this relational work.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing patient wishes, family concerns and a rapidly changing care situation.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, tolerate uncertainty and represent the patient's wishes in the team.
tasks.altitude: The nurse retains the same advocacy role and contact time.

reach.task: Help resolve an unmet patient concern
reach.learn: Consent, communication support and the local advocacy route

evidence.claim: Emotional support and advocacy depend on reciprocal conversation and contextual judgement.

assumptions: Boundary covers direct listening, support and advocacy, not a separately counted progress note or formal complaint investigation.
No structured feed is assumed. The nurse elicits needs and preferences in s1; interpreter or communication-support work, if needed, is unchanged outside this focal baseline.
Missing or conflicting preferences require further direct conversation in s1 and s2, not automatic inference.
Review native clinical-record access before adding tools; no new system or structured form is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the design introduces no new software or ongoing capture obligation.
Overlap with the family coping assessment task is not additive: a shared real conversation must be assigned once in a team roll-up.
unknowns: Communication-support access and current division of advocacy work
research_questions: Which requests fail to reach the responsible care-team member despite the existing handover route?

already_counted.description: Listening, support and advocacy remain fully human.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100, no incremental work, net=0. Routine reassurance and complex advocacy both keep their conversation time; no invented paperwork saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess family coping and decide whether intervention is needed

steps.what: Assess family adaptation and coping through conversation and observation
Determine whether family coping requires intervention and discuss next steps

tasks.design: Keep family assessment and intervention judgement with the nurse. Existing {OTHER} clinical records may provide care context, but an automated coping score does not replace speaking with the family.
tasks.previous_blocker: A family's coping cannot be reliably inferred from isolated text or a checklist alone.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change removes the assessment encounter.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing temporary distress from a need for additional support while respecting preferences.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret tone, context and changes over time and agree a sensitive support route.
tasks.altitude: No change to assessment responsibility or referral authority.

reach.task: Coordinate family support after an identified need
reach.learn: Referral criteria, consent and available support services

evidence.claim: Family coping assessment requires contextual nursing judgement and direct interaction.

assumptions: Boundary ends with the intervention decision and discussion; provision of specialist family support is outside and unchanged.
The nurse produces observations and family preferences during s1. No pre-existing structured coping category or free capture step is assumed.
Unclear answers require follow-up conversation, already retained in the assessment effort; no extraction model or automated intervention is proposed.
Test existing clinical-record assessment fields before any future custom form; this design adds none.
Zero incremental upkeep because the task remains unchanged.
Time overlapping emotional support or a general family conversation must be allocated once, not added across task estimates.
unknowns: Local assessment instruments and referral responsibilities
research_questions: What additional information changes a nurse's family-support decision in observed practice?

already_counted.description: Assessment and intervention judgement remain counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Whether needs are clear or require further discussion, the design removes no encounter or judgement time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise and monitor unit nursing staff

steps.what: Observe nursing staff practice and discuss workload and care concerns
Coach nursing staff and resolve or escalate supervision concerns

tasks.design: Keep practice observation, coaching and intervention with the supervising nurse. Native {OTHER} clinical-record and {HCM} staffing views can provide context, but their existing runtime earns no new saving in this direct supervision task.
tasks.previous_blocker: A workload count does not establish whether care is being delivered safely or staff need help.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing staffing views can support a supervisor without replacing bedside knowledge.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe practice early and giving useful feedback under pressure.
tasks.human_edge: Judge competence and workload in context and intervene constructively.
tasks.altitude: Supervision and escalation rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Support a colleague's supervised clinical development
reach.learn: Coaching, competence assessment and local escalation limits

evidence.claim: Unit nursing supervision includes observation, contextual assessment and coaching that a staffing dashboard does not perform.

assumptions: Boundary covers direct supervision, not roster production, payroll or a formal employment investigation.
The supervisor produces supervision findings through observation and staff discussion in s1. No structured competence or risk score is presumed.
Any existing roster is produced by the staffing coordinator outside this boundary with unchanged effort; missing context is resolved directly with staff within retained supervision time.
Evaluate native staffing and clinical-record views first; no additional dashboard, employee scoring or data capture is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because this design retains the existing process and introduces no monitoring system.
unknowns: Actual supervisory remit and whether preparation is a distinct measured part of this task
research_questions: Does direct observation reveal a recurring information lookup that can be reduced without shortening supervision?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Stable staffing and high-pressure shifts both retain direct supervision; no assumed admin baseline is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: This batch retains bedside care, family support and direct supervision. It does not grant new treatment or employment powers.
reach: Coordinate patient and family support with a patient representative
Support colleagues through practical clinical coaching
role.ambitious_version: A nurse with more reliable care context who remains responsible for bedside judgement and human support; this batch alone releases no measured time.
